items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: I would draw your attention to the possibility of making such an analogy, for instance, between Bix and Thomas Wolfe, who fundamentally were from the same origins and developing the same kinds of attitudes and reactions, using similar symbols, although each in a different idiom.

ctx.x: I would not make the same analogy between Bix and Fitzgerald, however, even though there were certain superficial similarities, but I don't think that anybody would contend that they were, for artistic purposes, the same. But I would draw your attention to the possibility of making such an analogy, for instance, between Bix and Thomas Wolfe, who fundamentally were from the same origins and developing the same kinds of attitudes and reactions, using similar symbols, although each in a different idiom.

Mm-hmm. Well, I have never, I have not read enough of Thomas Wolfe to know, but I know that you had mentioned that Bix's music conjures up to you the idea of the American dream, something about the American dream. That's right. That's right.
